business_scope.primary_industry_name: Stevedoring and Loading/Unloading of Bulk Cargo at Marine Docks

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–EU Bilateral Agreement on Trade in Goods (1972, in force)
Switzerland–United States Treaty of Friendship, Commerce and Navigation (1850)
Comprehensive Swiss DTA network covering more than 100 jurisdictions, OECD/BEPS compliant

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA; SR 955.0), Federal Ordinance on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLO; SR 955.01), Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) Art. 697i–697l, and FINMA Circular 2020/01.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity card for each shareholder, director, and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office / competent civil registry authority of country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or commercial register extract of corporate shareholder, if applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of parent entity's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized articles of association executed before Swiss notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial act under Swiss law (no apostille required)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening of all shareholders, beneficial owners, directors, and senior managers against Swiss SECO sanctions lists, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list, and EU/European Council sanction lists at KYC onboarding, annually, and upon any material change. Enhanced due diligence required for politically exposed persons pursuant to AMLA Art. 4(3) and FINMA Circular 2020/01. Screening results must be documented, risk-rated, and retained for 10 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft name must be expressed in an official Swiss language (German, French, Italian, or Romansh) or a permissible transliteration using Latin script. The name must not be misleading, must distinguish from all existing registrations, and may include abbreviations only when explicitly provided in the articles of association.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the cantonal commercial registry office within 20 days, attaching revised proposed names and legal arguments. If rejected again, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Cantonal Administrative Court (Verwaltungsgericht) within 30 days, and ultimately with the Federal Administrative Tribunal, pursuant to Art. 741 of the Swiss Code of Obligations and cantonal procedural regulations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole statutory seat for a port stevedoring AG. A physical registered office in the canton of incorporation is mandatory. A virtual office may be used for administrative support functions only, and the company must maintain operational substance at a licensed marine cargo terminal.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: initial physical inspection is mandatory for stevedoring licence issuance under ISPS Code and Swiss port security regulations; subsequent unannounced customs and safety inspections are estimated at 35% annual probability for a newly incorporated AG in this sub-sector.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), arts. 620-675 governing Aktiengesellschaft/stock corporation; Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV), arts. 18-58; Swiss Merger Act insofar as applicable; AutoCAD not applicable. Formation is governed by federal corporate law while registration is administered at cantonal level.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) of the registered office, acting through the Swiss Federal Commercial Register portal and Zefix central business index.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public notarial deed of incorporation (öffentliche Beurkundung der Statuten / acte constitutif notarié) and Commercial Register registration application (Anmeldung zur Eintragung).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Swiss AG minimum issued share capital is CHF 100,000. At formation at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up in cash, being 20% of the nominal value on each share and not less than CHF 50,000 in aggregate. The bank executes a blocking confirmation on a licensed Swiss bank account held in the future company's name; no separate state escrow account is required before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company is fixed at [street and number], Zug, Switzerland, and that the corporate purpose includes stevedoring, bulk cargo handling, terminal operations and all related logistics in accordance with ISIC 5224. RESOLVED, that the subscription and payment of the statutory share capital of CHF 100,000, evidenced by the bank blocking certificate, be and hereby is ratified. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed Chairman of the Board and [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, each with single signatory authority, and that all necessary Commercial Register filings, regulatory applications and operational license proceedings be authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve corporate name and obtain blocked capital confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug and a licensed Swiss bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a Zefix name search to confirm that 'CH AG' is distinguishable from all existing Swiss entities. Prepare the draft articles of association. Open a blocked bank account in the name of the future corporation and deposit at least CHF 50,000 of paid-up capital. The bank issues a capital deposit confirmation for use in the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (Statuten)
Passports or identity documents of founding shareholders
Bank account opening forms and Basel-based AML/UBO declarations
Name reservation application or preliminary Zefix name search result
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for insufficient distinctiveness, revise the corporate name with counsel and resubmit. If the bank capital confirmation is deficient, obtain a corrected confirmation from the bank before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial certification and execution of deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public in the canton of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding shareholders and the first members of the board appear before the Swiss notary. The notary verifies identity, statutory compliance, share subscriptions and paid-up capital. The shareholders sign the public deed and the notary attests the incorporation. The notarized deed is then delivered to the Commercial Register Office.
required_dossiers: Final signed articles of association
Identity documents of shareholders and board members
Original bank blocked capital confirmation
Declaration of beneficial ownership under Swiss anti-money laundering rules
Valuation report for any non-cash contribution, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a formal defect in the deed or capital evidence, cure the defect by supplemental notarial declaration or amended articles and resubmit for execution. Re-execution can occur on the same day if all parties remain present.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold first board meeting and adopt corporate governance resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of CH AG
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting. Adopt the First Board Resolution fixing the registered office, ratifying subscription of capital, appointing the Chairman, Chief Executive Officer and Company Secretary, and determining signing powers. Issue a certified extract of the board minutes for the Commercial Register filing.
required_dossiers: Notice and minutes of the first board meeting
Declarations of acceptance from directors and officers
Notarized incorporation deed
Identity and background information for each appointed officer
Specimen signatures or certified electronic signature records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer declines the appointment, the board shall meet immediately, appoint a replacement and ratify all prior management and filing acts. The corrected extract of minutes is then submitted to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office through the Swiss Federal Commercial Register portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, certified board resolution extract, bank capital confirmation, specimen signatures and statutory declarations through the official electronic filing interface or the cantonal registry. The registry reviews legal compliance under the Swiss Code of Obligations, enters the company in the Commercial Register and triggers publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce. Legal personality is acquired on registration.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation
Certified extract of the First Board Resolution
Specimen signatures of directors and authorized signatories
Original bank capital confirmation
Signed registry application form (Anmeldung zur Eintragung)
Statutory declaration that no shares were issued to illegally obtained funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register issues a deficiency letter or interim refusal, submit amended documents and written explanation within the statutory cure period. If registration is refused, appeal to the Federal Commercial Register Supervisory Authority or competent cantonal court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, social insurance and port authority notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), cantonal tax authorities, AHV compensation office, SUVA and Basel-Stadt Port Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After legal registration, apply for a Swiss UID/VAT number, register as an employer with the AHV compensation office and SUVA accident insurance, and notify the Rhine port operator of the company's terminal activity. Commence or continue applications for the terminal operating license and environmental permits.
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register extract
Value added tax (VAT/UID) registration form
Employer registration form for AHV/Social insurance
Accident insurance registration with SUVA
Port berth or terminal concession application
Corporate bank account confirmation for operational payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, voluntarily disclose and apply for late registration, referencing any cooperative compliance programs. If port concession priority is lost, resubmit through the port authority's formal berth allocation process and request an expedited review based on terminal-readiness evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Department of Economic Affairs Basel-Stadt, Port Authority Rheinhäfen Basel, in coordination with Swiss Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (BAZG) and Swiss Federal Office of Transport (BAV) where navigable-water interfaces are involved.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Terminal Operating License for Marine Dock Stevedoring and Bulk Cargo Handling (Betriebsbewilligung für Hafenumschlag und Stevedoring)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/Bundesamt für Umwelt BAFU) and the Cantonal Office for Environmental Protection Basel-Stadt (Amt für Umwelt Basel-Stadt)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA/UVP) under the Swiss EIA Ordinance (UVPV) for large bulk transshipment installations above the statutory throughput threshold; for smaller terminals, an environmental preliminary screening and permit procedure is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV), Swiss Clean Air Ordinance (LRV), and the Ordinance on Handling Waste (VVEA). Terminal stormwater and process water must be treated; suspended solids are to be reduced so that no turbidity plume enters the Rhine. Dust-generating bulk handling and conveyor operations must be enclosed or suppressed to meet PM10 and dust fallout limits, and all VOC-bearing operations must remain within LRV air emission ceilings.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the cantonal building inspectorate and professional fire brigade, structural load inspection of quay aprons, crane bases and heavy equipment zones, occupational health clearance under the Swiss Accident Insurance Act (UVG), work permits for stevedoring personnel, and harbor security vetting of terminal staff by BAZG and cantonal police.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV) / Administration fédérale des contributions (AFC) / Swiss Federal Tax Administration. Portal: www.estv.admin.ch; electronic VAT filing via ePortal (www.eservice.estv.admin.ch). Cantonal and communal tax authorities are separately competent for cantonal/communal income taxes and nexus registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a resident Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (CH_AG): after notarial incorporation and entry in the Commercial Register (Handelsregister/Zefix), the Swiss Federal Statistical Office assigns a Swiss Business Identifier (UID, complete: CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx). VAT registration (MWST-Nr.) is applied for separately with ESTV once taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 or if the AG voluntarily opts into VAT. Notification of VAT liability is filed electronically via the eVAT e-service; cantonal tax registration occurs automatically through the Commercial Register notification. Foreign entities with a Swiss permanent establishment obtain a UID and VAT number through a written application to the competent cantonal tax authority or ESTV and may need a UK-style? For Switzerland, a foreign entity with a permanent establishment must appoint a Swiss fiscal body; no mandatory fiscal representative is required within the EU concept.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss tax law does not provide a check-the-box system. A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft is inherently subject to entity-level taxation (corporate income tax at Federal, Cantonal, and Municipal levels). Available statutory elections: 1) VAT group election (Mehrwertsteuergruppe) under Art. 21 VAT Act, allowing a Swiss VAT group to be treated as a single taxable person; 2) election under the Swiss participation relief regime for qualifying dividends and capital gains; 3) request for formal ruling on hybrid mismatch treatment or entitlement to treaty benefits. Federal and cantonal levels do not allow consolidated fiscal filing of income tax; each entity is assessed separately.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA / VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 (exclusive of VAT) of annual turnover from taxable supplies in Switzerland; reverse-charge services from abroad are generally not counted for threshold but may trigger registration if received by a Swiss taxable person from a non-Swiss supplier, Art. 34 Swiss VAT Act (as of 2025 threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or an authority-approved tax clearance API for VAT transactions. A standard electronic VAT return is submitted via the ePortal (eService eVAT). There is no national mandatory e-invoicing or continuous transaction control. The Swiss QR-bill is a standard payment slip, but it is not a tax clearance instrument. VAT invoices must satisfy Art. 26 VoVAT (VAT Ordinance) irrespective of paper or electronic form.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Stevedoring, cargo handling, and terminal services performed on goods intended for export from Switzerland qualify for 0% VAT (unechte Steuerbefreiung / export zero-rating), provided that all the following conditions are satisfied: (i) the services are directly related to movable goods that are physically transported by a Swiss customs export procedure (Ausfuhrverfahren / export procedure); (ii) the goods are actually exported outside Switzerland and the export is evidenced by a customs export declaration; and (iii) the performance is either supplied at the Swiss port terminal for export or rendered to a non-Swiss recipient, without any nexus with domestic eventual consumption. Services related to the import of goods are not zero-rated, except for goods temporarily under customs supervision. The provider must retain complete export documentation to substantiate zero-rating and recover input VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss customs export declaration (Zollausfuhranmeldung / e-dec or ECW) evidencing the export movement and declaring the destination of the goods
Waterway Bill of Lading, Rhine bill of lading or equivalent intermodal transport document covering the terminal-to-vessel leg and the export carriage
Commercial contract and stevedoring/terminal service agreement confirming the export nature of the cargo handling
Inward remittance certificate (bank payment confirmation) or equivalent proof of settlement from the foreign importer/customer
Authorized customs officer stamp or electronic export certificate in the Swiss customs system (as required for VAT verification)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss tax and customs authorities conduct cross-verification between customs export declarations and VAT accounts, including B/L supporting documents and goods movement status. Unsupported zero-rating is reclassified as taxable supply at the standard rate of 8.1%; the supplier becomes liable for the VAT, default interest (currently around 4.5% per annum, recalculated at ordinary banking rates), and administrative fines under Art. 96-99 of the Swiss VAT Act. Intentional or wilful evasion of Swiss VAT through false export declarations attracts a fine up to three times the tax evaded, retrospective clawback may extend up to 10 years from the end of the year in which the supply occurred, plus criminal proceedings before the Federal Administrative Criminal Court. Stevedoring companies are specifically flagged for export verification of port inventories and Bayle? and any discrepancy is scrutinized against the terminal's electronic stock records and cargo manifest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB), established under the Federal Act on the Swiss National Bank (Nationalbankgesetz, NBG). The SNB is the monetary authority, manages the Swiss franc (CHF), and acts as a lender of last resort; foreign exchange intervention is permitted only for monetary policy purposes. There is no separate foreign exchange control administration; the SNB, in coordination with the Federal Department of Finance (FDF) and State Secretariat for International Financial Affairs (SIF), sets regulatory guidance. Switzerland is not a member of an anti-money laundering regulatory union beyond FATF, but FINMA supervises banks for AML compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully and freely convertible. Both the current account and the capital account are liberalized; there are no statutory exchange controls, no restrictions on the purchase or sale of foreign currency, and no prior licensing requirements for cross-border capital transactions. Profit remittances, dividends, repatriation of equity, interest payments, and royalties may be paid abroad without FX approval, subject only to general Swiss tax law, including withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends and interest if applicable, and to commercial documentation requirements under anti-money laundering rules. Treaty-based tax relief or refunds are available to eligible non-residents. No requirement exists to maintain any portion of export earnings in CHF or with a domestic bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Swiss law imposes no surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion, and no holding period on export proceeds. Receivables from exports can be held in any convertible currency, freely invested abroad, or repatriated without exchange control authorization. For statistical and balance-of-payments purposes, payments above CHF 15,000 received from abroad and settlement in foreign currency must be reportable to the Swiss National Bank by the account-holding bank, but the exporter is not required to file directly. No forced sale of export currency proceeds to the SNB or a licensed bank exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account / Capital Escrow Account (CHF multi-currency)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for primary treasury, Medium as a backup collection/disbursement channel. Swiss licenced fintech companies (FINMA banking-type licence under Art. 1b of the Swiss Banking Act) may offer deposit-taking up to CHF 100 million without full banking licence, but they are mostly retail-oriented. Foreign electronic-money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise and Revolut are not licensed as banks by FINMA; they may operate via Swiss bank partners or hold client funds with licensed banks, but they cannot offer insured corporate accounts or handle capital escrow for a Swiss port terminal company. A Swiss bulk stevedoring terminal should not rely on offshore digital EMIs for statutory capital escrows, LC settlement, or FX hedging; use a regulated Swiss bank as the enduring home.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an Aktiengesellschaft (AG) with Swiss resident directors, most tier-1 Swiss banks permit onboarding via remote video identification (FINMA-compliant) instead of a physical bank visit, provided digital identification is performed by a licensed trust service and the bank's risk appetite accepts the procedure. For non-resident directors or ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), physical appearance is commonly required, either at the bank's office or at a Swiss embassy/consulate with notarized signatures and passport certification. Private banks and larger universal banks may waive physical visit for OECD-resident entities, but the bank will always require a legalized corporate extract, copy of articles of association, proof of registered office, certified resolutions of the board on account opening, and passport copies of all signatories. The final mandate is bank-specific; no national statutory rule mandates personal appearance for every case, yet the anti-money laundering due diligence standard requires verification of identity from reliable, independent source documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO resides in a jurisdiction with enhanced FATF or Swiss FDF sanctions risk (e.g., non-transparent holding structures, offshore trusts, shell-company indicators).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organisational chart with every intermediate entity and final natural-person UBO; audited annual financial statements for the direct shareholder and beneficial owner; references from a regulated Swiss law firm or fiduciary on corporate purpose and source of funds; apostilled certificates of good standing for all upstream entities; clear explanation of commercial rationale for the Swiss AG and its connection to the port terminal; source-of-wealth declaration, bank references for the past 12 months, and tax confirmation of no adverse findings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow injections derive from a non-OECD jurisdiction with partial AML implementation or from a jurisdiction with high-risk commodities shipping exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written equity contribution resolution certified by the board; underlying commercial contracts (charter party, stevedoring service agreement, terminal management agreement); bank account statements showing the origin of funds; bill of lading or customs manifests proving the physical cargo dealing; declaration of no politically exposed persons (PEPs) among shareholders; consent from the Swiss port authority for the terminal concession; an independent external audit/assurance on the funding chain if funds exceed CHF 1 million.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer shares or historical bearer share issuance within the capital structure, even if already converted to registered shares.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current share register (Aktienbuch) listing all registered shareholders with full name, address, date of birth, and nationality; certificate from the company secretary that all bearer shares have been annulled or converted per the Swiss Code of Obligations; extract from the commercial registry (Handelsregisterauszug) confirming issued share capital and link to registered shares; for legacy bearer shareholders: copy of notarized transfer agreements and declaration of final UBO; proof of valid payment of stamp taxes, if any.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or potential sanctions list match on a port-terminal contractor, shipping line, or chartering counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screenshots of real-time sanctions screening output (OFAC, EU, UN, SECO) for all counterparties; due diligence file on the specific vessel ('know your vessel' - IMO number, flag registry, ISM code, P&I insurance certificate); copies of port authority permits and security certifications (ISPS code); confirmation that no goods are embargoed under Swiss or UN regimes; a system-implemented negative news monitoring protocol and response policy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder loan funding must be routed through a licensed Swiss bank using standard SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for interbank transfers. Since Switzerland does not apply foreign exchange controls, the payment purpose is described as 'capital contribution / share capital increase' (Erhöhung des Aktienkapitals) or 'shareholder loan' for loans. The transferring bank's purpose code should correspond to direct investment (for FDI statistics). The receiving Swiss bank must confirm the beneficial owner and the underlying board resolution. For amounts above CHF 10 million (or equivalent), banks generally request the opening of a capital escrow account under a notary's instruction when the capital increase is registered with the commercial registry; the notary is legally required to confirm availability of funds. The payment should be accompanied by a signed board resolution, the capital increase notarization plan, and prospective financial statements. The bank will perform a plausibility check of source of funds before crediting; no SNB authorisation is required. Funds must be available in the currency of accounting; if in EUR or USD, the bank will convert to CHF at commercial FX rate or hold in multi-currency account as per a standing instruction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For business-to-business settlements in stevedoring and port terminal services, the primary clearing rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfer for high-value or cross-border payments, especially to foreign vessels, nautical service providers, agents and port authorities; (2) MT202 COV for bank-to-bank cover payments if routed through an intermediary; (3) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EUR payments within the SEPA area, which is highly efficient for coastal and EU port-service invoices; (4) CH-clearing or CH-EUR for domestic currency clearing, operated by SIX Group. For trade-related disbursements such as bunker fuel procurement, cargo handling equipment purchases, or charter hire, commercial documentary instruments are used: irrevocable at-sight letter of credit (UCP 600), standby letter of credit (ISP98) in favor of the beneficiary, and documentary collection (CAD / D/P) with a Swiss bank as the advising or confirming bank. Payment terms should be net 7/14/30 days depending on disposable liquidity. The Swiss entity should establish an electronic banking mandate allowing two-signatory authorisation for amounts above CHF 250,000, and should use ISO 20022 payment messages where possible to carry structured remittance information, such as invoice number, contract ID, and port terminal reference.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contract (linear OTC contract, deliverable in CHF; no premium paid upfront; standard in Switzerland with 1-month up to 12-month tenors).
FX swap (spot leg plus forward leg between CHF and EUR/USD; used for rolling short-term liquidity and cash-flow management without counterparty limit concerns).
Cross-currency swap (long-dated, for matching ECB or USD floating rate obligations on terminal infrastructure loans; requires ISDA and CSA documentation).
Vanilla FX option (call or put on EUR/USD/CHF; premium paid upfront; permitted for hedging a known overseas capex invoice; mandatory per FINMA derivatives rules if embedded in structured product).

NDF (non-deliverable forward) is not necessary for CHF because the CHF is fully convertible with a liquid onshore market; a few domestic banks may restrict NDFs due to unclear legal table but it is not generally illegal. This instrument is listed as technically permissible under Swiss free-market law but ordinarily avoided for treasury straight-through processing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax, net wealth tax and profit distribution tax returns of the Swiss AG
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) and cantonal tax administration of the registered seat
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after financial year-end as per Swiss direct tax practice; many cantons fix 30 June for a 31 December year-end, with extensions by filed request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on underpaid corporate taxes and procedural fines up to CHF 10,000 for failure to file or incomplete returns; cantonal tax authorities may estimate taxable income if no return is submitted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT return (quarterly or annual declaration depending on elected accounting period)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 60 days after each calendar year end for annual VAT return; quarterly returns are due 60 days after each quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine under Swiss VAT Act Art. 102 up to CHF 10,000 for procedural violations, plus default interest on tax assessed; late-filing may trigger tax re-assessment by the ESTV

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting resolution approving the financial statements, profit appropriation, discharge of directors and changes to director signatory powers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss commercial register files certified resolutions when capital or articles are amended; ordinary AGM resolutions are kept in the statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months from close of financial year (Art. 699 Swiss Code of Obligations, CO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic administrative fine; any shareholder may request the court to convene the AGM at the company's costs and directors are liable for any resulting loss

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory audit report (ordinary or limited audit) including the annual financial statements and board report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of AGM; copy retained by the audit firm and corporate files
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed before AGM; report is normally issued within three to four months after financial year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If a mandatory auditor is not appointed, commercial register may set a compliance deadline; violations by responsible directors may be prosecuted as administrative offences with fines up to CHF 10,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register and shareholder register updated with share transfers and UBO confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Commercial Register and the statutory register filed with the corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Share transfers must be brought to the register of members and UBO data file with commercial register within 30 days of transfer; annual AGM confirms register accuracy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties up to CHF 10,000 for deliberate false registrations; intentional inaccurate UBO filings may lead to criminal prosecution under Federal Register Law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal or confirmation of port terminal stevedoring licence and operator concession
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal port authority / Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS) for Rhine port facilities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Set by concession deed; usually on anniversary date of licence or by 31 December of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inability to operate stevedoring services; concession may be restricted, suspended or withdrawn and administrative fines may be imposed for unauthorized port operation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit is mandatory when any two of CHF 20m total assets, CHF 40m turnover and 250 average employees are exceeded for two consecutive years; a limited review is required when two of CHF 4.5m total assets, CHF 9m turnover and 10 employees are exceeded; below these thresholds a unanimous shareholder opt-out may dispense with audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss GAAP in Code of Obligations Arts. 958–963; IFRS mandatory for public interest listed entities and may be adopted voluntarily; special disclosure rules for large groups

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The UBO identification data must be filed with the Swiss Commercial Register on initial registration and updated within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership; there is no separate annual UBO return; the common annual confirmation is the AGM review of the register of members and board acknowledgement of accurate UBO data

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $1,500–$5,500 for a Swiss trustee/secretariat covering registered office, register maintenance, compliance calendar and AGM support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,000–$20,000 depending on ordinary audit, limited review and entity complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Swiss federal corporate income tax 8.5% levied on net profit after tax (equivalent to 4.25% effective rate on pre-tax profit); combined federal + cantonal/communal effective rate approximately 11.9% in the Canton of Zug and ranging nationally from about 11.9% to 21.0% depending on canton.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific statutory tax holiday or preferential deduction exists for stevedoring, port terminal, or logistics-scope activities in Switzerland. General reliefs applicable to a Zug-domiciled AG include: (i) cantonal R&D super-deduction commonly at 50% of qualifying R&D costs, capped at 80% of taxable profit in certain cantons; (ii) notional interest deduction (NID) on qualifying surplus equity, adopted in Zug; (iii) participation relief (Beteiligungsabzug) exempting qualifying dividend income; (iv) tax-neutral revaluation / step-up planning upon acquisition of operational assets including cranes, conveyor systems, and dock machinery; (v) high hidden-reserve front-loaded depreciation practice approved by the tax authorities for movable and immovable port infrastructure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined cantonal and federal direct tax return for legal entities ('Steuererklärung juristische Personen' – Canton Zug / Federal Administration), covering federal direct tax (DBG), cantonal income tax, and cantonal capital tax in one filing package; e-filing through the Canton Zug portal 'taxonline' (https://www.taxonline.zg.ch) and ancillary annex submittals via the Federal Tax Administration portal (www.estv.admin.ch); mandatory attachments include signed statutory financial statements, tax reconciliation schedules, participation-claim forms, NID computation, and TP documentation summaries where relevant.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (business/fiscal year; most Swiss AGs align to the calendar year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax return must be filed within 6 months after the balance-sheet date (e.g., a 31 December year-end requires filing by 30 June of the following year); interim self-assessed quarterly installments are payable throughout the year and the final tax balance becomes due upon issuance of the assessment order (Veranlagungsverfügung); extensions are granted only upon written reasoned request and do not suspend default-interest accrual.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered corporate identity: legal name, legal seat, commercial register number (FOSC / CHE number), Swiss UID/IDE/IWG tax number, purpose clauses, board members, and shareholders with shareholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder group must disclose the ultimate beneficial owner chain with full registered addresses; a domestic UID number must be obtained for the Swiss AG; absence of a Swiss registered office or board secretary contact will flag the filing as non-substantive.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A – Erfolgsrechnung (Profit and Loss Reconciliation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory profit before tax from the audited or reviewed financial statements, including stevedoring service revenue, demurrage and handling fees, terminal storage charges, subcontracted labor costs, and crane/machine depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue from overseas vessel services must be recognized in the Swiss books only to the extent the services are performed through the Swiss AG's personnel and equipment in Switzerland; foreign permanent-establishment income, if protected under a DTA, must be separately disclosed and excluded from the Swiss taxable base to avoid double taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 01 – Jahresgewinn laut Handelsbilanz (Commercial Net Profit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the net profit per the signed commercial balance sheet; this is the starting point for all tax reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The figure must reconcile exactly with the published annual accounts; any mismatch with the audited financial statements submitted to the Swiss commercial register triggers automatic referral to the tax investigation unit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 02 – Aufrechnungen / nicht geschäftsmässig begründete Kosten (Add-backs of Non-Business Costs)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses: hidden profit distributions, excessive director fees, interest on tax underpayments, fines, bribes/kickbacks, political donations (non-deductible portion), and non-arm's-length related-party charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any recharged head-office or parent-company cost that lacks a written cost-sharing/transfer-pricing agreement and supporting invoice must be added back here; otherwise the amount is reclassified as a deemed dividend subject to 35% Swiss withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable income after profit adjustments, loss carryforward utilization, participation relief, NID, R&D deduction, and tax-exempt foreign PE income allocation; this amount is then split between the federal (4.25% effective pre-tax basis) and cantonal/communal assessment bases.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders cannot influence this figure in the return; the Swiss board of directors signs under criminal-liability declaration confirming arm's-length measurement of all cross-border service, leasing, and financing flows inside the port supply chain.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Capital Tax Box – Steuerbares Eigenkapital (Cantonal Capital Tax Base)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report share capital, legal reserves, retained earnings, and hidden reserves forming the Zug cantonal capital-tax base, after exclusion of qualifying participations and IP assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders' paid-up capital contributions have no special exemption; the AG must file a complete equity roll-forward reconciliation to avoid double assessment on repatriation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or refusal to file a corporate tax return triggers procedural fines ('Ordnungsbusse') of up to CHF 10,000 per instance plus periodic default surcharges; the tax administration may impose estimated assessments by discretion; late payment interest runs at the statutory rate of 4.5% p.a. for federal direct tax (cantonal default interest at 4.5%–5%); intentional false filings escalate to tax evasion proceedings under DBG Art. 175–176 with fines of 25%–100% of the evaded federal tax and potential imprisonment, in addition to full restitution plus interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal dividend withholding tax ('Verrechnungssteuer') applied at the source to gross cash dividends and all distributions in kind to shareholders of a Swiss AG.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Under the Switzerland–China Double Taxation Agreement (DTA, as revised by Protocol 2013, in force 1 January 2014): a China-resident company owning at least 25% of the voting shares of the Swiss AG receives a 5% final withholding tax rate; all other shareholders receive 10%; the paying Swiss AG must file for relief-at-source with the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) using form 82/83 series; the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Resident Certificate (TRC) issued by the Chinese State Taxation Administration for the relevant calendar year, complete the beneficial-ownership certification, and submit the dossier to ESTV within the 3-year limitation period following the dividend due date; the claim is rejected where the shareholder fails the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test (PPT) or lacks substance in China.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss statutory withholding on royalties is 0% (no Swiss WHT on IP royalties in either direction); for a Swiss AG paying royalties to a Chinese parent, Switzerland imposes no WHT, but China may assert source tax — reduced to 5% under the DTA (domestic rate 10%). On interest, Swiss statutory WHT of 35% applies only to interest on Swiss-issued public bonds and domestic bank deposit interest; ordinary intercompany credit interest is exempt from Swiss WHT; Chinese-source interest WHT on payments to Switzerland is 10% under the DTA (same as Chinese domestic rate). All treaty reductions require TRC and beneficial-ownership proof.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CHF 5,000,000 annual volume of cross-border related-party transactions generally triggers the practical expectation that a Swiss legal entity maintain a full OECD Local File; a group Master File is expected where worldwide consolidated revenue reaches CHF 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Reporting is mandatory for groups with consolidated revenue of at least CHF 900,000,000; contemporaneous arm's-length documentation must nevertheless be maintained for all intercompany transactions regardless of these thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not maintain a statutory Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to UAE or Caribbean offshore centers; however, the Swiss Federal Direct Tax Act (DBG), the BEPS Multilateral Instrument (MLI) principal purpose test, and the Federal Supreme Court anti-abuse doctrine (including the 141 II 447 substance jurisprudence) require real economic presence: permanent physical office, operative decision-making by the Swiss board, employment of operational and supervisory staff, independent invoicing and bank accounts, and actual execution of stevedoring, cargo-handling, and equipment-management functions in Switzerland; failure to satisfy economic substance voids treaty benefits, recharacterizes income as hidden profit distributions, and may invalidate the canton Zug tax ruling or NID claim.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally filing false or incomplete tax returns, suppressing stevedoring turnover, using fictitious subcontractor invoices, diverting port handling fees to undisclosed foreign bank accounts, or materially overstating deductible related-party costs to reduce Swiss taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under DBG Art. 175, a fine of 25%–100% of the evaded federal tax plus default interest; cantonal fines levied in addition; VAT evasion under the Swiss VAT Act (MWSTG) exposes the company to a fine of up to three times the evaded VAT; aggravated tax evasion involving more than CHF 100,000 of evaded tax per fiscal period is punishable under DBG Art. 176 with imprisonment of up to two years or a monetary penalty, in addition to full repayment, confiscation of hidden assets, and revocation of the Swiss port operating license where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false tax returns are personally subjected to the same criminal fines and imprisonment exposure as the company; boards cannot hide behind corporate personality where the tax return is knowingly false; Swiss courts pierce the veil and order civil restitution of misappropriated monies under Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 754; travel bans (Ausreisesperre) and passport denial may be imposed by the investigating magistrate to secure collection of evaded taxes and fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Zug AG as a pure invoicing shell without physical premises, staff, independent management decisions, or actual stevedoring operations in Switzerland; systematically using a 1,000 CHF nominal capital structure; shifting the entire Chartering and cargo-handling execution to a Chinese parent while booking artificial margin in Switzerland solely to gain DTA benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Federal Tax Administration denies all DTA relief (dividends, interest, royalties), recharacterizes the artificially retained profit as hidden profit distribution, and reimposes 35% withholding tax on the deemed distribution; additional fines of up to 100% of the reassessed tax, 10-year statute of limitations for undisclosed facts, interest, dissolution proceedings, and blacklisting of the entity by the commercial register for abusive incorporation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors cannot claim limited liability where the company is considered an artificial sham; they face personal joint and several liability for the full deficient tax, restitution orders, criminal conviction under DBG Art. 176 second paragraph, and judicial travel bans where non-resident board members are under investigation; the corporate veil is pierced where corporate assets are used for private shareholders' benefit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Channeling cash port fees, bunker surcharges, or stevedoring draughts through unlicensed third-country accounts; deliberately concealing the provenance of funds received from sanctioned counterparties; falsifying Swift wire transfer purposes; structuring deposits to circumvent Swiss anti-money-laundering reporting obligations under the AMLA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Pursuant to Swiss Criminal Code Art. 305bis, money laundering is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years or a fine of up to CHF 500,000 for gross-negligence complicity; aggravated laundering in connection with a criminal organization carries imprisonment of up to five years; the assets involved are confiscated by the State; FINMA may issue a professional ban against entities acting in the financial-services perimeter; the Stevedoring terminal operating license is revoked upon conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: CEOs, CFOs, and compliance directors are prosecuted personally for willful or grossly negligent conduct; they are excluded from future board service in Switzerland, face immediate travel bans to prevent flight, and remain personally liable for restitution of laundered proceeds under unjust-enrichment principles; medical, familial, and diplomatic privileges provide no shield against extradition on Swiss arrest warrants.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure / Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting non-arm's-length low-function marker prices for port unloading services, paying excessive management fees and commissions to the Chinese parent group, neglecting contemporaneous Local File documentation, failing to benchmark labor-heavy stevedoring rates against independent comparable terminal operators, or manipulating the docking and demurrage revenue split between Swiss and Chinese entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration applies discretionary upward adjustments, denies deductible related-party costs, and reassesses taxable income with default interest; the 10-year assessment period applies for undeclared facts; penalties of up to 40% of the adjusted tax liability can be stacked onto the adjustment, and any disallowed expense or margin is reclassified as a deemed dividend subject to 35% withholding tax; the entire Zug NID and participation-relief claims may be revoked retroactively.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving or signing flawed transfer-pricing documentation become personally exposed to fines and imprisonment on an ancillary tax-evasion charge; on audit failure, the Canton Zug fiscal authorities impute willful negligence to the responsible managers, attach personal bank accounts, and impose travel bans until full covered liability is secured; Swiss jurisprudence holds the responsible officer jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax deficiency when the officer signed with knowledge of the underlying TP distortion.
